pumac-2018-combinatorics-a-06.prompt: Michael is trying to drive a bus from his home, $(0,0)$ to school, located at $(6,6)$. There are horizontal and vertical roads at every line $x=0,1,\dots,6$ and $y=0,1,\dots,6$. The city has placed 6 roadblocks on lattice point intersections $(x,y)$ with $0\le x,y\le6$. Michael notes that the only path he can take that only goes up and to the right is directly up from $(0,0)$ to $(0,6)$, and then right to $(6,6)$. How many sets of 6 locations could the city have blocked?

pumac-2018-combinatorics-a-08.prompt: Let $S_5$ be the set of permutations of $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$, and let $C$ be the convex hull of the set $$\{(\sigma(1),\sigma(2),\dots,\sigma(5))\mid\sigma\in S_5\}.$$ Then $C$ is a polyhedron. What is the total number of 2-dimensional faces of $C$?
